name: @projexlight/sdk-scheduling
summary: Calendar, booking & no-show engine (P14·E2) re-homed from projex_crm calendar.service as a reusable, tenant-scoped, persona-keyed SDK. Hosts define reusable meeting types (15/30/45/60 min with buffers) and per-weekday business hours in an IANA timezone; the engine generates timezone-correct open slots and books appointments with double-booking prevention. A shareable public booking link (Calendly-style slug) lets an anonymous external invitee self-book, confirm and cancel using a high-entropy capability token — never a raw appointment_id — through an allowlisted /api/scheduling/public/ surface. The full booking lifecycle (confirm / reschedule / cancel), RFC 5545 ICS invites, an append-only booking-event timeline, timed reminder fan-out (24h/2h/15m), no-show detection with rescue rebooking, and two-way calendar provider sync (Google / Microsoft / CalDAV) round out the surface.

endpoints.description: Public render-the-page payload for a booking link; an unknown, inactive or expired slug is an indistinguishable 404.
Public open slots for one date (YYYY-MM-DD) on a booking link, enforcing the link's min-notice / max-days-ahead window server-side.
Anonymous invitee books a slot on a link; returns the appointment plus the capability token they use to confirm or cancel later.
Confirm a publicly booked appointment using only its capability token; an unknown token returns 404 without revealing whether the token or the appointment was wrong.
Cancel a publicly booked appointment using only its capability token, with an optional reason.
Create a reusable meeting type (name, slug, duration and booking buffers) for a host; slug is unique per tenant (409 on conflict).
List the tenant's meeting types.
Upsert a host's per-weekday business hours (weekday 0-6, start/end wall-clock time in an IANA timezone); re-setting a weekday overwrites the rule.
List a host's availability rules for the tenant.
Compute timezone-correct open slots for a host on a date, bounded by business hours and with already-booked windows removed.
Book an appointment for a host with double-booking prevention (409 on overlap) and an end-after-start check (400).
List a tenant's appointments, filterable by host, subject, status and start-time window.
Fetch a single appointment by id for the tenant; 404 when absent.
Confirm a pending appointment, advancing its lifecycle status and stamping confirmed_at.
Reschedule an appointment to a new start/end window, re-checking overlap and incrementing the RFC 5545 ICS sequence.
Cancel an appointment with an optional reason, stamping cancelled_at.
Return the appointment's RFC 5545 ICS invite as a text/calendar attachment for the current state.
List the append-only booking lifecycle timeline (created/confirmed/rescheduled/cancelled/notified) for an appointment.
Create a shareable public booking link binding a host + meeting type to a globally-unique slug (409 on conflict).
List the tenant's scheduling links.
Fetch a single scheduling link by id for the tenant; 404 when absent.
Schedule the reminder fan-out (default 24h/2h/15m, or custom offsets) for an appointment; idempotent per (appointment, offset).
List the scheduled reminders for an appointment.
On-demand drain of due reminders (claims pending rows past remind_at and fires the notifier); also runs on a timer when the worker is enabled.
On-demand no-show scan marking confirmed appointments past end_time + grace as no_show so a rescue rebook can be offered.
Rescue-rebook a no-show or cancelled appointment into a new confirmed slot, re-checking overlap and end-after-start.
Bind a host to an external calendar provider (google|microsoft|caldav) via an sdk-connectors install for two-way sync.
List the tenant's calendar connections, optionally filtered by host.
Fetch a single calendar connection by id for the tenant; 404 when absent.
Run a two-way sync for a connection (push unmapped appointments, pull provider changes); 422 with remediation on a provider error.
Push a single appointment to a connection's external calendar (propagating create/update/cancel to the mapped provider event).

models.description: Reusable bookable meeting kind (name, per-tenant-unique slug, duration and before/after buffers, location type). Referenced by availability slotting, appointments and scheduling links so a host offers a fixed menu of meeting kinds.

Per-weekday business hours for a host (weekday 0-6, start/end TIME) in an IANA timezone with a slot interval; a weekday with no active rule is a closed day (zero slots). One rule per (host, weekday) — upserted.

A booked calendar slot (parity: calendar_appointments) keyed on host_persona_id and optional subject_persona_id, overlap-guarded per host for double-book prevention. Carries lifecycle status/timestamps, ICS uid + RFC 5545 sequence, no-show/reminder bookkeeping and a nullable public_token capability for anonymous confirm/cancel.

Shareable public booking link (Calendly-style) binding a host + meeting type to a globally-unique slug, with a booking window (max_days_ahead, min_notice_minutes) and optional expiry, so an external invitee can self-book.

Append-only booking lifecycle timeline — one row per transition/notification (created/confirmed/rescheduled/cancelled/reminded/completed/no_show/notified) — powering booking history and the notification audit.

A single scheduled pre-meeting reminder for an appointment (e.g. 1440/120/15 minutes before), unique per (appointment, offset). A worker claims due pending rows (remind_at <= now) and fires the notifier.

Host-to-external-provider binding (Google Workspace / Microsoft 365 / CalDAV) via an sdk-connectors install, holding sync direction, delta cursor (sync_token) and status for two-way calendar sync. Unique per (host, provider, external calendar).
Appointment-to-external-event id mapping (one per connection + appointment) with etag and last-write direction, so reschedule/cancel propagate to the right provider event and echo loops are guarded.

scenarios.title: Define a meeting type and a host's weekly business hours
scenarios.when_to_use: When onboarding a host so the availability engine can generate bookable slots — you need at least one meeting type (duration + buffers) and per-weekday hours in the host's timezone.
scenarios.expected_outcome: A meeting_type row exists with the per-tenant-unique slug, and five availability_rule rows (one per weekday, upserted) bound the host's bookable window. Weekends have no active rule and are treated as closed days with zero slots.

scenarios.title: Anonymous visitor books a slot through a public link
scenarios.when_to_use: When an external prospect (no tenant login) needs to self-book against a host's availability via a shared Calendly-style link, receiving a capability token to manage the booking.
scenarios.expected_outcome: The public /book route (allowlisted, no auth) creates a confirmed appointment source='public_link' inside the link's booking window and returns a high-entropy public_token. The slot is now double-book-protected, and the token is the sole key for later confirm/cancel — a raw appointment_id will not work.

scenarios.title: Visitor cancels their booking with the capability token
scenarios.when_to_use: When the anonymous invitee needs to cancel the appointment they booked, using only the token issued at booking time (no tenant JWT, no appointment_id).
scenarios.expected_outcome: The appointment matching the token is cancelled (status='cancelled', cancelled_at set, reason recorded) and a booking_event is appended. An unknown or non-public token resolves to null, which the route maps to a 404 that leaks nothing about token validity — preventing IDOR/enumeration.

compliance_posture.notes: Stores PII of external, unauthenticated bookers (invitee name, email, notes) alongside timezone and meeting metadata, so appointment/booking_event data falls under GDPR data-subject scope. The public booking surface is anonymous: confirm/cancel are gated ONLY by a high-entropy per-booking public_token (never a raw appointment_id) to prevent IDOR, and unknown links/tokens return an indistinguishable 404 to block enumeration. Every appointment is tenant-scoped and persona-keyed; the booking_event timeline is append-only for audit. Booking implies invitee consent to be contacted for reminders; two-way calendar sync exports appointment data to external providers (Google/Microsoft/CalDAV) via sdk-connectors OAuth grants — treat that as a cross-processor data flow.
